hook: SCP-5999 is a long Halloween horror file built from seven chapters, each written as a different section of a containment report. Content note: it includes sexual assault and murder, dismemberment, the deaths of children, suicide and a lot of graphic gore. The page warns you not to continue and then opens anyway in a reduced format; that framing, and the short line that pushes you forward between chapters, are part of the effect.
whyItMatters: Its co-authored, esoteric-class and meta tags show in the build: each chapter fills one slot of a standard SCP entry (procedures, description, exploration, interview, timeline, test log, evidence) and carries its own in-story credit. Each slot also borrows a different horror subgenre, so the file doubles as a tour of the genre stitched into the Foundation format. Reading is treated as part of the procedure, which makes the reader complicit rather than a spectator.
thingsToNotice:
The first chapter sets the rules: every Halloween seven abducted civilians are dropped into the sealed Albright Manor to witness PROCEDURE SEVENFOLD, the observers are gassed with sarin afterward, and chains in the cellar hold something down. Seven chapters, seven witnesses, and the interstitial line keeps getting pushier, so you are being counted among them. The motifs then thread through every chapter: the phrase "This is where I died," the weakening chains, the nursery tune with rewritten lyrics, and Jacqueline Holcroft, raped, murdered and dismembered by six men in 2006, whose reburial disembowels every mourner and leaves her victims sterile and missing children.

Cresh Glen's exploration log kills an entire task force in set pieces: a twin dragged underground and pinned to a pole, a flogged corpse spelling the phrase, the squad leader crucified in a church, and a giant face made of bodies. The exorcism ends with the possessed agent, who had been reciting the Lord's Prayer backward, finishing a Bible verse in unison with her tormentor, an ambiguous surrender. The 1988 game timeline escalates from numb hands to a Game Over sound playing across seventy Foundation sites and senior staff hanged by ropes; the doll chapter reveals the doll as Cindy, one of the vanished twins, questioning a D-class about Holcroft while the log stops calling him a person and ends up filing him as an object. The last evidence list frays into repeated candle entries whose trailing words ask what could have happened to the bodies, and the page closes on a frantic order to turn off your device.
